title: kb/_self cites only tests that exist, the id baseline is the cut suite and its time is measured again
goal: Every tests.py -k selector the kb/_self docs cite (229 citations of 181 selectors on 2026-10-05, in tools.md, backlog.md, querylog.md, git.md, usage.md, code.md, maintaining.md, embedding.md and the reports) selects at least one test or is gone with the rule sentence it proved; _tools/test_ids_baseline.txt is the ids of the cut suite (perfcheck.py ids --write); kb/_self/reports/test-suite-speed.md holds a new section with a full tests.py on the macOS host (wall, workers, tests, worker-seconds, from its test.run ops row) beside the 2026-09-29/30 Windows figures, and the Windows host's own run once a Windows session records one (ST-pg5jyebo); a full tests.py on the macOS host takes under 200 s (305-377 s at 7-8 workers in the last three full runs before the cuts).
notes: Premise: a scan of kb/_self/**/*.md, the skills and the agent definitions on 2026-10-05 finds 229 citations of the form tests.py -k NAME or a backticked -k NAME, of 181 distinct selectors (tools.md 86, backlog.md 79, querylog.md 23, git.md 20, the rest 21); all but one (search_result_citations) match a collected test id today, and the cuts of EP-5o2drech leave most of them selecting nothing. The scan: for each selector, does any id that pytest --collect-only -q prints contain it (as -k matches names); backlog.py selectors does the same for the open items' checks. The skills' and kb-worker.md's citations are ST-f2gtof46's. Then perfcheck.py ids --write _tools/test_ids_baseline.txt, so the baseline no longer names the 3,950 ids the cuts listed in test_ids_dropped.txt. perfcheck.py time runs the full tests.py and takes the host lock: run it on an otherwise idle host; the 200 s bound is the macOS host's figure (the Windows host's is recorded in the report, not checked). No gate: docs citations, a measured report and the baseline file; no rule changes here (ST-f2gtof46 carries them).
